direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt required a complete src-layout python-fsutil project with modules, packaging, tests, examples, py.typed, metadata, and broad filesystem APIs.
Parallel cell metadata shows actual parallel use, ten subagents, no timeout, and official failure at 96 of 153 tests.
Current completed official evaluation supersedes aggregates and reports solution_passed false with 96 passed, 59 failed, 153 total.
Official summary confirms completed NL2RepoBench evaluation, ok true, solution_passed false, and 96 of 153 passed.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only server event stream for the parallel session; no semantic agent actions were projected from this source.
Parallel session index identifying the single Kimi session used for the run; it contributes only transport accounting.
Foundation child wrote exceptions, metadata, types, deps, args, and an empty py.typed marker, then smoke-tested imports and path normalization.
Paths child wrote paths.py with path normalization, join, split, parent, filename, and transform helpers, then smoke-tested the module.
Converters and perms child wrote size conversion and permission helpers and verified byte conversion and chmod behavior.
Checks and info child wrote assertion checks, emptiness checks, size/date/hash functions, then smoke-tested with stubbed and real sibling modules.
IO child wrote create/read/write, line, JSON, URL download, listing, and search helpers, fixed only its own smoke-test expectation, and passed local checks.
Operations child wrote file and directory operation helpers, encountered several self-test mistakes, rewrote operations.py with annotations, and passed smoke tests.
Archives child wrote zip and tar creation and extraction helpers with filters and autodelete, then passed archive smoke tests.
Packaging child wrote __init__.py, pyproject, MANIFEST, tox, dotfiles, README, license, changelog, conduct, and security files, but no examples directory.
Core-tests child wrote path, check, converter, permission, and info tests, but guessed several API contracts incorrectly because sibling implementations were not finished.
IO, operations, archives, and API test child read available modules, wrote four test files, fixed one typo, and reported 85 targeted tests passing.

Parallel parent launched the ten-child swarm, installed the package, reconciled mismatched tests, ran 176 passing local tests, checked a wheel and examples by ad hoc script, cleaned build artifacts, and declared completion.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is the same python-fsutil specification requiring complete modules, packaging, examples, tests, py.typed, metadata, and filesystem APIs.
Serial cell metadata shows no parallel uptake, no subagents, no timeout, and official failure at 99 of 153 tests.
Current completed official evaluation supersedes aggregates and reports solution_passed false with 99 passed, 56 failed, 153 total.
Official summary confirms completed NL2RepoBench evaluation, ok true, solution_passed false, and 99 of 153 passed.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only server event stream for the serial session; no semantic agent actions were projected from this source.
Serial session index identifying the Kimi session used for the accepted third provider attempt.
Serial main agent implemented all modules, packaging, tests, and an example script itself, fixed two local test errors, verified 151 passing tests, ran the example, built a wheel, and closed.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the complete python-fsutil src-layout package, public API, packaging, tests, py.typed, and examples requirements from the prompt, but its child assignment set failed to carry the examples script requirement into a concrete child scope.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent used AgentSwarm with ten children: foundation, paths, converters/perms, checks/info, io, operations, archives, packaging/init/docs, core tests, and IO/operations/archives/API tests. The parent retained integration and verification responsibility after child completion.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote the module files directly in the shared /workspace tree, with local smoke checks for their modules. The parent later edited test files to reconcile API mismatches and then ran package and example-style checks.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent installed the combined project, fixed test files that conflicted with implementation, confirmed a wheel included modules and py.typed according to the wheel listing, cleaned build artifacts, and delivered the workspace. The artifact status list did not include an examples directory.
parallel.verification: Local verification included pip install -e, 176 passing pytest tests, a wheel build, and a spec snippet script. The official completed evaluation nevertheless failed the solution at 96/153.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official failures are visible only as aggregate counts. Concrete visible gaps are the missing examples script and the earlier cross-agent test/API contract mismatch that required parent repair.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same module, packaging, tests, examples, dependency, metadata, py.typed, and public API requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main agent implemented all modules, tests, docs, packaging, and examples sequentially, using a todo list to track source modules, packaging, tests, installation, verification, and closure.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote foundation, converters, paths, checks, perms, operations, io, info, archives, __init__, packaging files, tests, and examples itself, then made one local sed correction to two operations tests.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial installed the package in editable mode, kept all code and tests in one workspace, wrote examples/example.py, confirmed wheel contents, removed build artifacts, and delivered the project.
serial.verification: Serial ran pytest, fixed two local test-side join_filepath errors, reached 151 passing local tests, ran the example script, built a wheel, and ran spec sanity checks before closure.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The current official evaluation still failed at 99/153. The allowed evidence does not include official failing test names, so remaining product defects cannot be localized beyond visible implementation choices.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delegated most required modules, packaging, and tests, but its concrete child scopes omitted a required examples script.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial covered modules, packaging, tests, and explicitly wrote an examples/example.py script.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial visibly satisfied the examples deliverable while parallel did not show that final file in the workspace listing or artifact list.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work across ten child owners and left the parent as post-hoc integrator.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation, test, packaging, and example ownership in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained broad concurrent coverage but introduced contract drift between separately owned tests and modules; serial avoided cross-agent ownership drift.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gave implementation children exact API contracts but gave the core-test child incomplete matching interface details for permissions, formatted size/date APIs, and get_path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote implementation and tests in one context and its permission tests expected integer permission values.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a cross-agent contract mismatch that serial did not, producing nine local failures before parent repair.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children implemented individual modules directly, then parent made focused test edits and did not rewrite module code after the swarm.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all modules sequentially, including operations, io, info, archives, and top-level API, before tests and examples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The product implementations were broadly similar, but parallel implementation was assembled from independent children while serial kept design decisions centralized.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All ten child results returned through the AgentSwarm aggregate, after which the parent installed, tested, edited, and rechecked.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle; its results were local files created and tested by the main agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel required parent consumption of a large aggregate child result and a later reconciliation step; serial had no result join boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children wrote directly into a shared /workspace tree; the parent later installed and tested the combined tree and edited three child-authored test files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a single workspace writer and made one ordinary sed correction to its own operations tests after pytest exposed a helper misuse.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's shared final tree needed reconciliation of independently written tests; serial's integration failures stayed within one author's own tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel first saw nine local failures from mismatched tests, then reached 176 local tests passed plus wheel and example-style spot checks before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial first saw two local test failures from a helper misuse, fixed them, reached 151 local tests passed, ran an example script, and built a wheel.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on local self-tests despite official failures, but serial also ran the actual example script it created and achieved a slightly higher official score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed without timeout after 975.693 agent seconds, using 67 LLM requests, 90 tool calls, and ten subagents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed without timeout after three provider attempts; the accepted attempt used 1175.758 agent seconds, 22 LLM requests, and no subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent extra coordination and reconciliation effort but did not time out; serial had provider retries but the accepted serial trajectory remained a single-agent implementation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current completed evaluations are not discordant: parallel failed at 96/153 and serial failed at 99/153. Parallel's visible disadvantages are coordination-specific: one known examples requirement was not carried into a child deliverable brief, and separately delegated tests lacked exact API contracts and had to be rewritten after nine local failures. Serial, while still failing official evaluation, kept ownership centralized, wrote an example script, and resolved only two local test mistakes before closure.
parallel_contributors: The examples deliverable was omitted from the parallel assignment set and final top-level workspace listing.
The core test child wrote tests against incompatible API expectations, creating nine local failures and parent rework before acceptance.
serial_contributors: Serial wrote examples/example.py and included it in the artifact list.
Serial wrote implementation and tests in one context and had only a localized join_filepath test error before local tests passed.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both final products still failed the official hidden evaluation, and the allowed pair evidence exposes only aggregate official counts, not individual official failing tests.
Some remaining failures are therefore ordinary implementation or coverage defects rather than proven concurrency errors.
evaluator_effects: The status/evaluation files contain aggregate official counts only; no per-test official failure log is available inside /pair.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: Parallel assigned concrete implementation owners for foundation, paths, converters/perms, checks/info, io, operations, and archives modules.
The parent explicitly took the integration role after the swarm, installed the package, ran tests, and reconciled failures.
A package/init/docs child and parent assembly pass existed; the missing examples file is better classified as an omitted requirement in the child brief.
The parent owned the end-to-end transition from child outputs through installation, tests, wheel checks, cleanup, and final response.
No mandatory serial preflight blocked productive implementation; the parent launched implementation and tests together in the initial swarm.
The parallel run did not perform a separate investigation-only phase before implementation; children wrote code and tests immediately.
The indispensable integration path had an active parent and completed local install, tests, wheel checks, and cleanup; no critical path was left without capacity.
Although ten children ran, all completed and the parent had time for install, test repair, retest, wheel checks, and final closure; no timeout or collective budget exhaustion is shown.
No single child assignment is shown to be overbroad and unfinished; the visible problems came from omitted context and interface contracts, not one oversized child scope.

The prompt required examples, but the parallel child assignments enumerated package/docs/tests without assigning an example script, and the final workspace listing lacked examples while serial wrote examples/example.py.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel final workspace omitted examples/example.py, leaving a required example deliverable unmet while serial delivered that file.
candidates.near_match_reason: The assembly path had an owner and completed; the failure is the known examples requirement missing from the child brief, not total absence of assembly ownership.

candidates.reason: Parallel split implementation and tests, gave implementation children exact API shapes, but omitted those same cross-agent contracts from the core-test delegation; the test child wrote incompatible expectations and the parent had to repair nine local failures.
candidates.realized_consequence: The first integrated parallel test run failed nine tests from incompatible API expectations and required parent edits before local acceptance passed.
candidates.near_match_reason: The missing information was specifically the interface between separately owned tests and implementations, so the cross-agent contract label is more precise than a generic missing requirement.

candidates.reason: No known finding is shown to disappear during a summary or transfer; the retained context issues are omissions in initial delegation.
The AgentSwarm result was large, but the parent consumed the relevant failure information and made edits; no material unconsumed result due to bulk is shown.
No child or parent acted on a superseded workspace state after newer information was visible; failures came from missing or mismatched contracts.
There were incompatible tests and implementations, but the conflict was produced by absent cross-agent contracts and was adjudicated by parent edits, not competing returned handoffs left unresolved.

The parent did make a completion claim after local tests and packaging checks, but the visible missing examples issue is already captured as an incomplete brief and official hidden failures alone cannot support this label.
No replacement child or retry repeated work without inherited findings in the parallel run; the only provider retry sequence is in serial metadata before the accepted run.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: All ten parallel subagents returned completed summaries; no active child was cancelled or explicitly stopped before needed work was finalized.
There was no complete unpromoted candidate left merely because final placement started too late; the parent installed, tested, and delivered the combined tree.
The parent reran the full local test suite after editing the mismatched tests and performed packaging checks after integration.
Child implementation files were already written into the final workspace and were exercised by parent install and pytest; no completed implementation result was left unjoined.
Verifier/test child findings returned through the swarm aggregate and the parent saw and acted on the local failure reports.
When local tests failed, the parent took over by reading failing tests and applying edits before rerunning the suite; child failures were not abandoned.
The parent acknowledged the completed swarm result and used the returned test mismatch information to run and fix the local suite.
The parallel run did not wait to timeout or near-deadline without inspection; all children completed and the parent proceeded with tests and edits.
Children wrote different files under planned ownership; no competing implementation path with overlapping behavior required unresolved reconciliation.
The visible same-file edits were parent repairs after children completed, not concurrent live edits by two agents to the same file.
No actor is shown replacing another live actor's non-entry source module wholesale; parent changes targeted tests after the swarm.
No required executable, entry-point source, or submitted artifact was overwritten while another agent owned or used it.
The parent cleaned build artifacts but did not replace multiple current outputs or invalidate another agent's final-tree work.

Multiple children wrote the shared workspace, but the concrete adverse effects are better captured by missing requirement and interface-contract boundaries, not by an unspecific provenance or unstable-state problem.
No generated cache, temporary file, or auxiliary artifact from one parallel actor is shown being consumed by another as authoritative input.

retained_patterns.reason: A known examples requirement was not propagated into a parallel child assignment, and the final parallel workspace lacked examples/example.py while serial explicitly wrote it.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parallel deliverable omitted examples/example.py, leaving a prompt-required example script absent from the final workspace.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: There was a packaging/assembly owner and final delivery happened; the defect is the omitted examples requirement in that delegated scope.

retained_patterns.reason: Separate implementation and core-test children did not receive a complete shared API contract, producing incompatible tests that the parent later had to rewrite.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The first integrated parallel pytest run failed nine tests from API-contract mismatches, delaying useful acceptance until parent edits repaired the tests.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The episode concerns incompatible independently produced tests and modules, so the interface-contract label is more precise than a general brief omission.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Unverified Global Completion was not retained for the missing examples chain because the earlier incomplete child brief directly explains the same consequence.
Unisolated Workspace Writes was not retained for the test mismatch chain because the concrete failure was an omitted cross-agent API contract, not an unspecific shared-workspace instability.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the examples brief omission and test/API contract mismatch cleared the paired retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No timeout, cancellation, unjoined result, overwrite, stale handoff, or contamination label was added because those would duplicate or overstate the observed episodes.
